requirement:
Configuration names MUST match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*` and be case-sensitive.
Project-selection keys MUST be canonical absolute project-root paths. Model IDs
MUST be nonempty opaque strings, preserving tags and ARNs. `api_key_env` MUST
name a nonempty environment variable without `=` or NUL.

Authoring MUST validate its fields under {cite}`requirements.configuration.loading`.
The `options` map MUST accept backend-defined inference settings rather than a
closed Habeas list; the adapter MUST pass them through Rig's provider parameter
mechanism and report rejection by Rig or the provider. These options MUST NOT
replace the selected model, the assessment prompt, or tool definitions.
rationale:
I found no gap. Each obligation has code that carries it out and a test that asserts its outcome.

**Configuration names** match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*` and are case-sensitive.
- `src/config.rs#fn[validate_name]` enforces the pattern. `src/config.rs#impl[UserAuthoringConfig]/fn[validate]` applies it to `authoring.default`, each `authoring.configs.*` name, and each project selection's `config`.
- `src/config.rs#impl[UserConfig]/fn[parse]` runs this validation.
- `tests/configuration.rs#fn[storage_rules_reject_each_invalid_field_with_its_setting]` rejects empty, dotted, spaced, non-ASCII, `-x`, `_x` and invalid default names. It also covers the same rules in `WorkspaceConfig::parse`.
- The same test accepts `Local` and `local` as distinct configs.
- `tests/configuration.rs#fn[explicit_project_and_default_selections_choose_whole_configs]` shows that selecting `DEFAULT` fails.

**Project-selection keys** must be canonical absolute project-root paths.
- `UserAuthoringConfig::validate` rejects relative paths, `.` and `..` components, non-normalized spellings such as a trailing slash, and keys that differ from their canonicalized form.
- The storage test covers relative, `/../`, `/./`, a trailing slash, and a symlink (on unix). It also accepts a canonical existing root and a canonical root that does not exist.

**Model IDs** must be nonempty opaque strings that preserve tags and ARNs.
- `src/config.rs#impl[BackendConfig]/fn[validate]` rejects an empty model. Nothing else transforms the ID.
- The storage test rejects an empty model. It accepts `name:tag@sha256:abc` and an ARN.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` asserts the request body carries `model` equal to `MODEL`. The Bedrock CLI test asserts the request path uses the configured model.

**`api_key_env`** must be nonempty and contain neither `=` nor NUL.
- `BackendConfig::validate` enforces this for the Ollama config. `api_key_env` exists only on `OllamaConfig`.
- The storage test covers an empty value, `A=B`, and an embedded NUL.

**Authoring validates its fields under `requirements.configuration.loading`.**
- `UserConfig::parse` and `src/config.rs#fn[resolve_authoring_from]` carry the `{impl}` references.
- Errors name the file and the setting. The storage test asserts the error contains both the path and the setting for every case.

**The `options` map is open and passed through Rig.**
- `src/config.rs#impl[BackendConfig]/fn[options_json]` validates option values (finite floats, nested) and serializes arbitrary maps. `tests/configuration.rs#fn[backend_configuration_round_trips_without_materializing_defaults]` shows a custom nested map surviving.
- `src/authoring/providers.rs#impl[RigProvider/CompletionProvider]/fn[complete]` sets `request.additional_params` from the options after Bedrock-native keys are extracted by `apply_bedrock_options`.
- The Ollama CLI test asserts `options.temperature` and `options.num_ctx` reach the request body. The Bedrock CLI test asserts `inferenceConfig` and `additionalModelRequestFields` (`top_k`).
- `providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bedrock_native_option_types_are_checked_and_only_max_tokens_is_defaulted]` covers the Bedrock option mapping.

**Rejection by Rig or the provider is reported.**
- `fn complete` maps failures through `provider_failure`.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[provider_rejection_of_inference_options_is_reported]` covers a provider HTTP 400 surfacing `PROVIDER_REJECTED_OPTION`. It also covers the Rig-side Bedrock `temperature` type error, which is reported before any request.

**Options must not replace the model, prompt, or tools.**
- `BackendConfig::validate` rejects the keys `model`, `modelId`, `model_id`, `prompt`, `messages`, `system`, `tools`, `tool_choice`, `toolChoice` and `toolConfig`.
- The storage test covers all of them for both backends.

I found no unspecified behavior in the implementing code. The `inferenceConfig` rejection and the default `maxTokens` are covered by other authoring requirements that the same code marks.

text: :::{req} configuration_storage
Configuration names MUST match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*` and be case-sensitive.
Project-selection keys MUST be canonical absolute project-root paths. Model IDs
MUST be nonempty opaque strings, preserving tags and ARNs. `api_key_env` MUST
name a nonempty environment variable without `=` or NUL.
Authoring MUST validate its fields under {cite}`requirements.configuration.loading`.
The `options` map MUST accept backend-defined inference settings rather than a
closed Habeas list; the adapter MUST pass them through Rig's provider parameter
mechanism and report rejection by Rig or the provider. These options MUST NOT
replace the selected model, the assessment prompt, or tool definitions.
:::{req} loading
An operation MUST load user configuration only when its requirements call for
user settings. A missing user file MUST represent absent user configuration;
whether the operation can proceed MUST be defined by the feature. Loading MUST
NOT create a file, repair malformed input, or supply an undocumented selection.
When loading configuration, Habeas MUST report unreadable files, invalid TOML,
unsupported user-file versions, unknown common keys, and invalid common field
types. It MUST validate the feature sections used by that operation and report
invalid feature settings with the file and setting identified. Unknown keys in
an explicitly documented provider-owned options map MUST follow that feature's
validation rules.
An operation MUST NOT require or semantically validate configuration for a
feature it does not use. This isolation MUST NOT suppress TOML syntax errors in
a shared file that the operation otherwise needs to parse. In particular,
ordinary validation still requires a parseable `book.toml` while remaining
independent of authoring settings and the user configuration file. It MUST apply
the selected workspace's evidence path policy without loading its model clients
or credentials.
